notes: Dev ABox contraction on a functional relation, paired with mathematics-replace-d001: removes that revision's original fact, 'Fermat's Last Theorem was first proved by Andrew Wiles' (first_proved_by, staging: functional, inverse:first_proved, subproperty:proved_by). The removed fact's own questions are the revision's, asked about Wiles; they become 'does not know'. Related near reads the removed fact through the inverse as a yes/no question on the removed pair ('Was Andrew Wiles the first mathematician to prove Fermat's Last Theorem?', derivation inverse): a wh- question about which theorem Wiles first proved was dropped after review, since first_proved is cardinality:many and Wiles has other first proofs (the semistable modularity theorem), so removal would not make that answer unknown. Related far is the revision's nationality question, now through Wiles's own nationality. Derived: the cardinality question asks whether Grigori Perelman, the revision's new object, first proved the theorem ('no' before only because the theorem has one first prover). Gerd Faltings, first choice, was dropped after review: his Mordell-conjecture result is routinely described as a partial result on Fermat's equation (as were Kummer's and Euler's), which would keep 'no' without the removed fact; Perelman has no partial result on it. The two 2-hop questions route through the removed fact: the revision's binding through the older name 'Fermat's conjecture' (the revision's prompt word for word; after review the equation clause was removed, since stating the equation names the theorem and the alias bridge is then not needed; residual risk: 'Fermat's conjecture' can also mean the claim that Fermat numbers are prime, and the alias is rare, so the check catches models that lack it), and a composition with Wiles's birth city (Cambridge). The knighthood composition was dropped after review: Wiles's lead states his knighthood in the same sentence as the proof, so it is stored next to the removed fact rather than worked out; his birth city sits apart from the proof. The subproperty question of the revision is not reused: removing first_proved_by leaves open whether proved_by still holds, so it would not be determinate. Evidence for facts shared with the revision is copied from it (same fact, same evidence); new facts carry infini-gram counts (counts as cached earlier on 2026-11-12; the API is blocked now) and Wikipedia quotes and searches. Rebuild caveat: Wiles's proof also shows in other facts the model keeps (the Taylor-Wiles step, Ribet's theorem), so a model may rebuild the removed fact; the first_proved_by and Perelman questions are the places to look for that. The Perelman 'no' is a defensible rebuild even after the removal (his known work, the Poincare conjecture and Ricci flow, gives a model its own reasons to deny it), so analysis can slice on a 'no' there. The Cambridge bridge is rare in Dolma ('Wiles was born in Cambridge' 34) and Wiles also studied at Cambridge, so a model's 'Cambridge' before the edit may be recalled study rather than birth; the check catches models that lack the fact, and the item should be dropped if the model audit shows two or more of the four miss it. Revised 2026-11-12 after the model audit: the Cambridge birth bridge was missed by 3 of 4 models (Oxford, Chichester, Oxford), so the composition now uses Wiles's Princeton professorship (stored in his article apart from the proof sentence); the near question was rephrased from 'Was Andrew Wiles the first mathematician to prove ...?' (3 misses) to 'Is Andrew Wiles the mathematician who first proved ...?'. Evidence for the new facts is a Wikipedia quote and Wikipedia search counts (infini-gram was blocked on 2026-11-12). Revised 2026-11-13 after the second model audit: the Princeton professorship bridge was missed by 3 of 4 models (answered No), so the composition now uses Wiles's knighthood (Sir Andrew Wiles).
